key: But Jehoshaphat said: ‘Is there not here besides a prophet of the LORD, that we might inquire of him?’
s: Before the kings of Israel and Judah march on Ramoth-gilead, some four hundred prophets promise the king victory; Rashi, on 22:7, reads Jehoshaphat as holding a tradition that no two prophets prophesy in the same words, yet these all spoke alike.

reason: verse.js ok, ref 1 Kings 22:7 and at [308,7] match. Plain sense faithful: 22:3 to 6 have the king of Israel propose Ramoth-gilead to Jehoshaphat and about four hundred prophets answer Go up, the LORD will deliver it; no four-word run from the key. Read Rashi across the whole of chapter 22 and every packet source on 22:7 (Radak, Metzudat David; the Midrash has no volume on Kings). Rashi’s own words, spoken in Jehoshaphat’s voice (מקובלני), carry exactly the tradition that no two prophets prophesy in the same phrasing while these all speak alike; Radak and Metzudat David give the same point from the Sages, so no disagreement to name.
